scope: Native filtered backend runtime ownership and nested-Tokio safety. Source edits restricted to native.rs; no native host operations.

implementation.ownership: NativeSearcher is an Option-owned wrapper around DiskIndexSearcher, replacing the internal alias without changing open_searcher/search call signatures.
implementation.construction: When a Tokio handle is detected, the entire construction operation runs on a scoped plain thread. Errors after inner-runtime construction therefore dispose that runtime outside the caller runtime.
implementation.query: Synchronous query and indexed-vector test query use the same scoped plain-thread fallback when a Tokio handle is detected. Outside Tokio, both use their direct inner call.
implementation.drop: Inside a Tokio context, Drop moves a ManuallyDrop-owned inner searcher to a plain disposal thread and joins it. Its worker panic is logged rather than propagated. Outside Tokio, destruction is direct.
implementation.resource_failure: If the OS cannot create a disposal thread, its closure cannot destroy the ManuallyDrop payload. The runtime is deliberately retained/leaked and the resource failure is logged, avoiding a nested-runtime destructor panic.
implementation.serving_detail: Handle::try_current also succeeds in Tokio spawn_blocking. The conservative sync wrapper may add a plain-thread hop in that context; ordinary std::thread query workers remain direct. An optimized async-serving integration is a separate root-owned API decision.

independent_lifecycle_smoke: The cpp_comparison agent reported a passing local 512-row actual-PQ/SSD smoke with 100 durable updates, 75 exact probes, compaction, reopen, old snapshots, and garbage collection after this wrapper. That agent/root own the reproducible smoke artifact and hashes.
performance_claim: No new performance claim; the standalone core benchmark continues to call DiskIndexSearcher directly, while the lifecycle smoke measures ordinary std worker queries.
